title: How the Internet Works — Trace a Web Request
description: Follow a web request from browser to server and back, understanding each network layer
objective: Students will use browser DevTools to observe real HTTP requests, analyze headers, status codes, and timing to understand how web pages load

steps.title: Open Browser DevTools — Network Tab
steps.instructions:
Open **Chrome** → press **F12** to open DevTools.

Click the **Network** tab.

Check **Preserve log** (so entries don't clear when the page navigates).

Now type `https://techpath.biz` in the address bar and press Enter.

Watch the Network tab fill up with entries. Each row is a separate HTTP request.

Note:
- How many total requests were made? (shown at bottom)
- How much data was transferred?
- How long did the page take to load? (DOMContentLoaded and Load times at bottom)

steps.title: Analyze the First Request
steps.instructions:
Click on the **first entry** in the Network list (it should be the HTML document).

Look at the **Headers** tab:

**General:**
- Request URL — the full URL
- Request Method — GET (retrieving data)
- Status Code — 200 OK (success), or 301/302 (redirect)

**Response Headers:**
- `content-type` — what kind of data (text/html)
- `server` — what web server (nginx, Apache, etc.)
- `content-encoding` — is it compressed? (gzip, br)

**Request Headers:**
- `user-agent` — your browser identification
- `accept` — what content types your browser can handle
- `accept-language` — your language preference

Screenshot the Headers tab.

steps.title: Identify Resource Types
steps.instructions:
Look at all entries in the Network tab. Filter by type using the buttons:
- **Doc** — HTML documents
- **CSS** — Stylesheets
- **JS** — JavaScript files
- **Img** — Images
- **Font** — Web fonts
- **XHR/Fetch** — API calls (data requests)

Create a table:

| Type | Count | Largest File | Size |
|------|-------|-------------|------|
| HTML | ? | ? | ? |
| CSS | ? | ? | ? |
| JS | ? | ? | ? |
| Images | ? | ? | ? |
| Fonts | ? | ? | ? |

Click the **Size** column header to sort by size. What is the largest resource? Could the page be optimized?

steps.title: Understand Status Codes
steps.instructions:
The Status column shows HTTP status codes:

| Code | Meaning | Example |
|------|---------|--------|
| **200** | OK — success | Page loaded correctly |
| **301** | Moved Permanently | URL changed, browser follows redirect |
| **304** | Not Modified | Using cached version (fast!) |
| **404** | Not Found | Broken link, missing page |
| **500** | Server Error | Something crashed on the server |

Now try loading a page that doesn't exist:
```
https://techpath.biz/this-page-does-not-exist
```

Watch the Network tab — you should see a **404** status code.

Try another site and look for **301** redirects — many sites redirect from `http://` to `https://`.

steps.title: Measure Loading Performance
steps.instructions:
Right-click any column header in the Network tab → enable **Timing** column.

Click on any request → click the **Timing** tab:

| Phase | What It Is |
|-------|----------|
| **DNS Lookup** | Time to find the server's IP address |
| **TCP Connection** | Time to establish connection |
| **TLS/SSL** | Time for encryption handshake |
| **Waiting (TTFB)** | Time until first byte from server |
| **Content Download** | Time to receive the full response |

Which phase takes the longest? For most sites, **Waiting (TTFB)** is the bottleneck — it's server processing time.

Now test with **Slow 3G** throttling:
- Click the gear icon (⚙️) or the throttle dropdown → select **Slow 3G**
- Reload the page
- Compare total load time

Reset throttling to **No throttling** when done.

**Submit:** Your complete Network analysis report with screenshots showing request count, headers, status codes, resource breakdown, and timing analysis.

expected_output: A detailed report showing browser DevTools Network tab analysis — request count, headers breakdown, resource types table, status code identification, and timing analysis comparing normal vs throttled loading
